content:
Former "Grey's Anatomy" star Isaiah Washington is mourning the loss of his wife and the mother of his children.

"Yes... the rumors are true. My wife of 29 years suddenly collapsed on May 31, 2025, and passed away on June 9, 2025," the actor shared in an emotional Instagram post on Sunday, referring to his late wife Jenisa.

"This has been an enormous shock for me and our entire family. She sadly passed away from a massive hemorrhagic stroke and never recovered," he said, urging fans to pay attention to their health.

"Listen to me, everyone... some headaches are not just headaches or migraines; the situation could be far more serious than you think, even a warning sign. If possible, please get a brain scan and take those headaches seriously," he said.

Washington then explained why it took him so long to publicly announce his wife's passing.

"She has been gone for 16 months, but she left behind three remarkable children who continue to carry on her spirit," he said. "I don't know if this is an appropriate post because Jenisa Washington valued her privacy deeply, but I suppose I'll just have to face her scolding in heaven someday."

The couple, who had been together for nearly three decades, had three children: Isaiah, Tyme, and Iman.

Washington was fired from the cast of "Grey's Anatomy" in 2007 after making anti-gay remarks backstage at the Golden Globes. He later spoke to HuffPost about the fallout from the incident.

"After the Golden Globes incident, everything fell apart. I lost everything, couldn't afford an agent... couldn't afford PR... couldn't afford to keep going," Washington said at the time.

He said being forced to pause his acting career made him "a better husband, a better father, and a better artist."

"Today, with a heavy heart and a slight sense of relief, I announce that I will be retiring early from the entertainment industry," he wrote. "Those who have been following/witnessing my journey on this Twitter since 2011 all know that I've done everything in my power to fight hard, but it looks like the haters, the instigators, and the useful idiots have ultimately won."

However, according to his most recent Instagram post, Washington appears to be returning to the big screen soon.
